classification.difficultyReason: Construct two ordered decompositions of each horizontal argument, adjusting translation distances and signs when dilation or reflection changes position in the sequence.

inlines.text: Each of the following is obtained from
using a sequence of transformations. For each rule, describe two possible sequences: (a) dilated, then translated; (b) translated, then dilated. Include a reflection in the

answer.short: Horizontally dilate by a factor of $\frac12$, then translate right $4$ units.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac12$ using $x\mapsto2x$, then translate right $4$ units using $x\mapsto x-4$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(2x)\\y&=f\bigl(2(x-4)\bigr)\\y&=f(2x-8)\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Translate right $8$ units, then horizontally dilate by a factor of $\frac12$.
answer.worked:
Translate right $8$ units using $x\mapsto x-8$, then dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac12$ using $x\mapsto2x$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(x-8)\\y&=f(2x-8)\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Horizontally dilate by a factor of $\frac13$, then translate right $1$ unit.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac13$ using $x\mapsto3x$, then translate right $1$ unit using $x\mapsto x-1$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(3x)\\y&=f\bigl(3(x-1)\bigr)\\y&=f(3x-3)\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Translate right $3$ units, then horizontally dilate by a factor of $\frac13$.
answer.worked:
Translate right $3$ units using $x\mapsto x-3$, then dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac13$ using $x\mapsto3x$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(x-3)\\y&=f(3x-3)\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Horizontally dilate by a factor of $5$, then translate right $35$ units.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by a factor of $5$ using $x\mapsto\frac{x}{5}$, then translate right $35$ units using $x\mapsto x-35$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{x-35}{5}\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{x}{5}-7\right)\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Translate right $7$ units, then horizontally dilate by a factor of $5$.
answer.worked:
Translate right $7$ units using $x\mapsto x-7$, then dilate horizontally by a factor of $5$ using $x\mapsto\frac{x}{5}$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(x-7)\\y&=f\left(\frac{x}{5}-7\right)\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Horizontally dilate by a factor of $3$, then translate left $6$ units.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by a factor of $3$ using $x\mapsto\frac{x}{3}$, then translate left $6$ units using $x\mapsto x+6$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{x+6}{3}\right)\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Translate left $2$ units, then horizontally dilate by a factor of $3$.
answer.worked:
Translate left $2$ units using $x\mapsto x+2$, then dilate horizontally by a factor of $3$ using $x\mapsto\frac{x}{3}$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(x+2)\\y&=f\left(\frac{x}{3}+2\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{x+6}{3}\right)\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
Horizontally dilate by a factor of $4$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $2$ units.

Factor the argument as $-\frac14(x-2)$.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by a factor of $4$ using $x\mapsto\frac{x}{4}$, reflect in the $y$-axis using $x\mapsto-x$, then translate right $2$ units using $x\mapsto x-2$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)\\y&=f\left(-\frac{x}{4}\right)\\y&=f\left(-\frac{x-2}{4}\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{2-x}{4}\right)\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
Translate left $\frac12$ unit, horizontally dilate by a factor of $4$, then reflect in the $y$-axis.

Use sequential substitutions to obtain $-\frac{x}{4}+\frac12$.
answer.worked:
Translate left $\frac12$ unit using $x\mapsto x+\frac12$, dilate horizontally by a factor of $4$ using $x\mapsto\frac{x}{4}$, then reflect in the $y$-axis using $x\mapsto-x$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(x+\frac12\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{x}{4}+\frac12\right)\\y&=f\left(-\frac{x}{4}+\frac12\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{2-x}{4}\right)\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
Horizontally dilate by a factor of $2$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $\frac23$ unit.

Factor the argument as $-\frac12\left(x-\frac23\right)$.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by a factor of $2$ using $x\mapsto\frac{x}{2}$, reflect in the $y$-axis using $x\mapsto-x$, then translate right $\frac23$ unit using $x\mapsto x-\frac23$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\\y&=f\left(-\frac{x}{2}\right)\\y&=f\left(-\frac12\left(x-\frac23\right)\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{2-3x}{6}\right)\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
Translate left $\frac13$ unit, horizontally dilate by a factor of $2$, then reflect in the $y$-axis.

Use sequential substitutions to obtain $-\frac{x}{2}+\frac13$.
answer.worked:
Translate left $\frac13$ unit using $x\mapsto x+\frac13$, dilate horizontally by a factor of $2$ using $x\mapsto\frac{x}{2}$, then reflect in the $y$-axis using $x\mapsto-x$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f\left(x+\frac13\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{x}{2}+\frac13\right)\\y&=f\left(-\frac{x}{2}+\frac13\right)\\y&=f\left(\frac{2-3x}{6}\right)\end{align*}$$
